title: The Shia adhan
hook: many Shia add a testimony that Ali is the wali of Allah in the adhan, which their scholars teach is recommended, not part of the shahada
carry: the call, as each hears it

segments.voice: Yesterday, riya', the hidden partner, and your line: only for him. Did your unseen deed stay unseen? Today, the testimony as it sounds in a Shia call to prayer. Day one thousand seventy-one.

Two recordings of the call to prayer, played one after the other. Allahu akbar, in both. I testify that there is no god but Allah, in both. I testify that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah, in both. Then, in the second recording, a line the first one doesn't have: ashhadu anna Aliyyan waliyyullah. I testify that Ali is the wali of Allah. A listener who grew up with the first call might hear it and wonder: is that a third sentence of the shahadah? Today, what Shia Muslims and their scholars say about it.

First, who says it. Ali was the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, Fatima's husband, a figure honored in Sunni and Shia tradition alike. For Shia Muslims he is also the first imam, the one they hold the Prophet appointed to lead after him. In the Shia call, a line about him comes right after the testimony to the Prophet. Second, what wali means. A friend, a protector, one close to God. A hadith recorded in Sunni collections, among them Tirmidhi's, has the Prophet say that whoever he is mawla to, Ali is mawla to him. Mawla, too, can mean friend or protector. Sunni and Shia readers understand that saying differently, and both keep it. Third, what Shia scholars teach about the line. They teach that it is recommended, and that it is not part of the shahadah. The testimony that makes someone Muslim is still the two sentences of this week. The line about Ali is said alongside, as an honoring, not as a third pillar of faith. Fourth, each call has its own shape. The Shia call also includes come to the best of deeds. The Sunni dawn call adds a line of its own: prayer is better than sleep. Each community has its reasons for its wording. That's the end of this week. We cleared the room with no god, filled it with but Allah, met the messenger, the new Muslim, the conditions, oneness from three sides, and the hidden partner. Today, the same testimony, called from two kinds of minaret.

The practice: listen to both adhans. Settle, and breathe. For this sit, call one of them to mind, any adhan you've heard, even once, even in a film. Hear it slowly in your memory, line by line: the greatness, the two testimonies, the invitation to prayer and to success. Notice which line stays with you. After the bell, find a recording of a Sunni call and a Shia call, and listen to both, all the way through, without comparing. Just hear what each one carries. The bell holds the time.
The Shia adhan. The call to prayer in its Shia form, with a testimony honoring Ali that their scholars teach is recommended, not part of the shahadah. Today's word.
Your line: the call, as each hears it. Today, listen to both recordings, and notice where they meet. Tomorrow, last words. Day one thousand seventy-one.

howItsDone: In Shia mosques the muezzin often adds ashhadu anna Aliyyan waliyyullah after the testimony to the Prophet and includes hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal; Shia jurists teach the line about Ali is recommended and not part of the adhan's required wording or of the shahadah.

notes: Editor: removed the uncited 'many Shia' count claims (teach, word, howItsDone) and the root/etymology claim linking mawla and wali (now a plain gloss of mawla).

Shia Keeper to check: the description of the 'third testimony' as recommended and not part of the adhan or shahadah follows the index; jurists differ on its exact status (some say it may be said with the intention of blessing, not as part of the adhan). Confirm the phrasing 'as an honoring' and 'first imam... the one they hold the Prophet appointed'.

Sunni Keeper to check: 'The Sunni dawn call adds a line of its own: prayer is better than sleep. and the framing of Tirmidhi 3713 as understood differently by Sunni and Shia readers. Confirm the hadith number.
'Mawla... a word from the same family' as wali (same root w-l-y); confirm.
The status of the line is stated as Shia scholars' teaching without naming a jurist; Keeper may add a named source.
'Many Shia include this line' follows the index's 'many Shia'. Week end (1065–1071) look-back is in the teach's closing lines.
No Qur'an quotation today; Qur'an 5:55 (guardian) was deliberately left out because Sunni and Shia readings of it differ and would need more room than one day.
